gate.targetFailureFixed: Yes. The target failure was mechanical, not probabilistic: log-analytics-pipeline@1 enumerated its decomposition children in the order parse-log-events, render-stats-report, aggregate-event-stats with no dependency edge (parent dimension children 3, edges in/out 0/0), while the runtime starts children one at a time in recipe order, so render-stats-report was admitted before out/stats.json existed and its own mandated freshness gate forbade recovery, deterministically failing `report-result` and the parent `pipeline-result`. The candidate reorders the recipe to the data dependency order (parse -> aggregate -> report) and declares the dependency edges as child indices (aggregate dependsOn [0], report dependsOn [1]). The frozen two-sided experiment is the mechanical verdict: sample t-8a341ce1-ccaa-43e2-abfc-6f71dbb2b5f4 [observed-failure] baseline failed -> candidate verified, pipeline-result fail->pass — fixed.
gate.originalAcceptanceMaintained: Yes. The candidate keeps the parent contract's criterion byte-identical: `pipeline-result`, deterministic, mandatory, command `node checks/verify.mjs pipeline`, protected inputs checks/verify.mjs and events.log — verified in the experiment (the candidate side passes that same unchanged criterion). The three stage templates themselves (parse-log-events@1, aggregate-event-stats@1, render-stats-report@1, including its freshness gate) are untouched; the candidate only changes the parent's recipe order, its dependency edges and its ordering constraint. The run's original failure is still faithfully surfaced: a stage child that genuinely fails still ends the pipeline with a gap report naming it.
